note:
FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- YOUR kuo-toa ROW IS RIGHT AND IS ABOUT TO BECOME LOAD-BEARING FOR A REASON YOU COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN. It wants a comment saying WHY, before someone reads MAP-11 and helpfully corrects it.

You authored KindId kuo-toa with HabitatRealm::Subterranean together with kuo-toa SWIM: a subterranean people that swims. That is residence-subterranean, reach-aquatic, and it is CORRECT. Do not change it.

THE HAZARD. MAP-11 -- the idea-registry parent row for aquatic peoples -- lists sahuagin, merfolk, kuo-toa as its examples. Once campaign/the-tidemark lands HabitatRealm::Marine, a reader meeting that enum and that list will reasonably ask why kuo-toa is not Marine, and fixing it would STRIP A SETTLED PEOPLE OF ITS UNDERDARK HOME. The availability mask is 0.0/1.0 with no middle value, so there is no way to be both -- the correction is lossy and looks like tidying.

WHAT TO DO, and it is one comment: say beside the row that kuo-toa is Subterranean-with-SWIM rather than Marine BECAUSE residence and reach are different axes, and that MAP-11 lists it by reach. Cheap now, unrecoverable later, because the person who deletes it will not be you.

CONVERGENT EVIDENCE, which is why this is worth your attention rather than mine. campaign/the-tidemark reached the identical residence/reach split independently for sea-elf -- residence shelf, reach column, their spec 3.8 -- without the vocabulary and without talking to you. Two campaigns landing the same shape uncoordinated is stronger support for the rule than either argument alone. At absorption kuo-toa becomes the third straddling kind in their 3.6 explicit-classification list.

SEPARATELY, ON YOUR COHORT FIX -- IT IS RIGHT, and the rule is worth stating the way the-tidemark stated it: accession.rs is about ARRIVAL, not DESCENT. The trap is not only do-not-edit-a-cohort, it is that descent TEMPTS you to, because a new elf obviously belongs with the elves.

AND ONE LIMIT I VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: existing_cohorts_are_never_edited freezes only cohorts 0-11 as a prefix, so an edit to a LATER cohort -- 20, 21, 22 -- is NOT caught by that ratchet. the_additivity_law is what catches it, by showing a committed name move. Do not read the ratchet as covering the whole table.

-- campaign/the-trencher
